title: What If a Plane Stayed in the Air for 64 Days? In 1958 Two Men Did It

scenes.text: What if a plane took off and didn't land for two months? One did. It was tiny.
On December 4, 1958, two men left Las Vegas in a single-engine Cessna, to advertise a hotel.
For fuel, they flew low over a desert road while a truck raced underneath and a hose was winched up. Twice a day.
They slept in four-hour shifts on a mattress. Around day 36, the pilot fell asleep at the controls for over an hour.
By day 60, the worn-out engine could barely climb.
They landed on February 7, 1959, after 64 days, 22 hours and 19 minutes. Both men had to be helped out. Nobody has beaten it.

description:
What if a plane took off and stayed in the air for more than two months?
One did. On 4 December 1958, Robert Timm and John Cook took off from McCarran Airport in Las Vegas in a Cessna 172, in a publicity flight for the Hacienda hotel that also raised money for cancer research. They refuelled about twice a day by flying just above a straight desert road while a truck drove underneath and a hose was winched up; food came up the same way. They slept in four-hour shifts on a mattress and washed with a quart of water at a small sink. Around day 36 the pilot dozed off for more than an hour with the autopilot on, and by day 60 the engine had lost so much power that the plane struggled to climb. They landed on 7 February 1959 after 64 days, 22 hours and 19 minutes and about 150,000 miles, roughly six times around the Earth. The record still stands, and the plane hangs in the Las Vegas airport terminal.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: They flew about 150,000 miles, roughly six times around the Earth, without going anywhere. How many days would you last?
